newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamatane Sec to close U.S. arm, merge Japan offices.
newsitem.headline: Yamatane Sec to close U.S. arm, merge Japan offices.

text.p: Yamatane Securities Co Ltd said on Friday it would close its U.S. subsidiaries and merge 13 offices in Japan to cut its network in Japan to 35 offices from 48 under a two-year restructuring programme that started this month.

The consolidation of the domestic offices will be made on June 2, 1997, while the closure of the U.S. subsidiary will be completed by the end of 1997/98, which ends on March 31, 1998, said Yamatane, a second-tier Japanese securities house.
It said, however, that it will maintain its Hong Kong and London-based subsidiaries.

It also said in a statement that it would aim to post a parent current profit of 1.6 billion yen on revenues of 18.0 billion yen in the business year ending March 31, 1999, under the two-year programme.
Yamatane sees a parent current loss of 7.9 billion yen in 1996/97 on revenues of 11.6 billion yen.
By the end of 1998/1999, it plans to cut its work force to 1,000 from 1,100 at the end of March 1997.

It said the programme, which includes streamlining its corporate structure to boost efficiency, is aimed at coping with expected liberalisation of stockbroking commissions under Japan's "Big Bang" reforms. The reforms aim to liberalise the nation's financial markets by 2001.
